Story: As a employee, I want to create a multi-line claim with category, amount, date and vendor and save it as a draft, so that I can build a claim over several days before submitting.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given I am logged in, When I create a claim with a title, Then it is saved in DRAFT and appears in My claims.
Given a DRAFT claim, When I add or edit lines (category from the fixed list, amount, date, vendor) and save, Then the lines and the total in en-IN rupees are shown.
Given a line with amount 0, more than ₹10,00,000, a future date or a date older than 365 days, or no vendor, When I save, Then I get a 422 with a message on that line and my data is kept.
Given a hotel line without city or with nights < 1, When I save, Then it is rejected with 422.

Story: As a employee, I want to upload a receipt photo or PDF for a line from my phone, so that finance has evidence without paper.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given I pick a JPG, PNG or PDF up to 5 MB, When I upload it, Then I get its id, filename, size and SHA-256, and can attach it to a line.
Given a file over 5 MB or another type (including a renamed .html), When I upload it, Then I get 422 and a clear message.
Given a receipt I uploaded, When another employee requests it by id, Then they get 404 unless they can see a claim using it.

Story: As a employee, I want to submit my claim and immediately see the policy outcome for each line with a reason, so that I know whether it is approved, needs approval, or must be fixed.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given a DRAFT claim with valid lines, When I submit, Then each line shows APPROVE, ROUTE or REJECT with rule code and message.
Given any line is REJECT, When I submit, Then the whole claim is AUTO_REJECTED with all reasons, and I can edit and resubmit.
Given no REJECT but any ROUTE line, When I submit, Then the claim is PENDING_APPROVAL at the first applicable step.
Given all lines clean and total ≤ ₹25,000, When I submit, Then the claim is APPROVED (or SAMPLE_AUDIT if sampled).
Given all lines clean and total ₹25,000.01, When I submit, Then the claim is routed, not auto-approved.

Story: As a finance auditor, I want meal spend to be limited to ₹1,500 per employee per day across all their claims, so that employees cannot split one day's meals across claims to stay under the limit.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given meals of ₹1,500.00 on one date, When submitted, Then the line is APPROVE.
Given meals of ₹1,500.01 on one date, When submitted, Then it is ROUTE with MEAL_DAILY_LIMIT.
Given ₹1,000 of meals on a date in an earlier non-rejected claim, When I submit ₹500.01 of meals for the same date in a new claim, Then it is ROUTE.
Given the earlier claim was REJECTED, When I submit, Then its meals are not counted.

Story: As a line manager, I want hotel, cab and weekend expenses that break policy to be flagged for my attention, so that I review only the lines that need judgement.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given a hotel in a tier-1 city (TIER1_CITIES, case-insensitive), When amount > ₹6,000 × nights, Then ROUTE with HOTEL_NIGHT_LIMIT_TIER1; exactly ₹6,000 × nights is APPROVE.
Given a hotel in any other city, When amount > ₹4,000 × nights, Then ROUTE with HOTEL_NIGHT_LIMIT_OTHER.
Given a local_cab line, When amount is ₹2,000.01, Then ROUTE with CAB_TRIP_LIMIT; ₹2,000.00 is APPROVE.
Given an expense date on Saturday or Sunday, When submitted, Then ROUTE with WEEKEND_SPEND; Friday is not flagged.
Business Rule / Decision Ref: HOTEL_NIGHT_LIMIT_TIER1; HOTEL_NIGHT_LIMIT_OTHER; TIER1_CITIES; CAB_TRIP_LIMIT; WEEKEND_SPEND; D6; D7

Story: As a finance auditor, I want lines without receipts above ₹500 and duplicate expenses to be caught at submit, so that we do not pay unsupported or duplicate claims.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given a line of ₹500.01 without a receipt, When submitted, Then REJECT with RECEIPT_REQUIRED_ABOVE; ₹500.00 without a receipt is APPROVE.
Given a receipt whose SHA-256 is already on another non-rejected line, When submitted, Then REJECT with DUPLICATE_RECEIPT_HASH.
Given the same vendor (case-insensitive, trimmed), amount and date as an earlier non-rejected line, When submitted, Then ROUTE with DUPLICATE_VENDOR_AMOUNT_DATE.
Given the seeded data, When the dashboard loads, Then planted duplicates appear in violations by rule.

Story: As a line manager, I want an inbox of claims waiting for me, oldest first, with flags and the receipt side by side, so that I can approve or reject quickly with a comment.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given claims at MANAGER step for my reports, When I open the inbox, Then I see them oldest first with employee, department, flags and age in hours.
Given a claim in my inbox, When I approve with an optional comment, Then it moves to the next step or APPROVED and the timeline records me.
Given a claim in my inbox, When I reject, Then a comment is required and the claim becomes REJECTED.
Given a claim that is not at my step, When I call the action API, Then I get 403.

Story: As a line manager, I want to send a claim back for clarification, so that the employee can fix it without starting a new claim, and nothing changed is paid without re-approval.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given a claim at my step, When I send it back with a comment, Then it becomes NEEDS_CLARIFICATION and the employee sees the comment.
Given NEEDS_CLARIFICATION, When the employee edits and resubmits, Then policy re-runs and the chain restarts from MANAGER, even if it had reached AUDITOR or HEAD.
Given a claim in PENDING_APPROVAL or APPROVED, When the employee tries to edit, Then they get 409.

Story: As a finance head, I want claims above ₹25,000 to need an auditor and claims above ₹1,00,000 to need me as well, so that large spend always gets finance review.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given a routed claim of ₹25,000.00, When submitted, Then the steps are MANAGER only.
Given ₹25,000.01, When submitted, Then MANAGER then AUDITOR.
Given ₹1,00,000.00, Then MANAGER then AUDITOR; given ₹1,00,000.01, Then MANAGER, AUDITOR, HEAD.
Given the claimant has no manager (or is their own manager), When submitted, Then MANAGER is skipped and AUDITOR is mandatory.
Given the claimant is the only head, When submitted, Then HEAD is skipped and audit log records head_step_skipped_self.

Story: As a line manager going on leave, I want to delegate my approvals to a colleague for a date range, so that claims are not stuck while I am away.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given I am a manager, auditor or head, When I create a delegation with a delegate and start/end dates, Then it is listed under given (mine) and received (theirs).
Given today is within the window (first and last day inclusive), When the delegate approves, Then it succeeds and the timeline reads 'approved by delegate on behalf of me'.
Given today is outside the window, When the delegate acts, Then 403.
Given I choose myself as delegate, When I save, Then 422.
Given I delete the delegation, When the delegate acts, Then 403.

Story: As a finance head, I want nobody, including a delegate, to approve their own claim, so that segregation of duties holds.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given I am a manager with my own claim, When I open the inbox, Then my claim is not there, and calling approve on it returns 403.
Given I am a delegate and the claim is mine, When I try to act on it as the delegator, Then 403.
Given an auditor's own claim in SAMPLE_AUDIT, When they try to clear it, Then 403.
Business Rule / Decision Ref: D9; D10; CLAUDE.md 'Nobody approves their own claim'

Story: As a finance auditor, I want a review queue with filters and bulk approve, so that I can clear many routine high-value claims quickly.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given claims at AUDITOR step, When I filter by kind, department, category, flag, amount range or text, Then only matching rows show.
Given I select several claims, When I bulk approve with a comment, Then each claim gets its own result (ok/error), and failures do not undo successes.
Given an employee or manager calls bulk approve, Then 403.
Given two people approve the same claim at the same moment, Then exactly one succeeds and the other gets 409.

Story: As a finance auditor, I want a random 10% of auto-approved claims held for sample audit before payout, so that auto-approval is spot-checked before money leaves.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given a claim that auto-approves and is selected by sha256(claim_id:salt) % 100 < SAMPLE_AUDIT_PERCENT, When submitted, Then it becomes SAMPLE_AUDIT, not APPROVED.
Given 10,000 claim ids and 10%, Then about 10% are selected and the same id always gives the same answer.
Given a SAMPLE_AUDIT claim, When I clear it, Then APPROVED; when I reject it, Then REJECTED.
Given a SAMPLE_AUDIT claim, Then it is not in the payout eligible list.

Story: As a finance head, I want to put approved claims into a payout batch, export a bank CSV and mark the batch paid, so that employees are reimbursed once and only once.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given APPROVED claims not in a batch, When I create a batch, Then they move to IN_PAYOUT atomically.
Given a claim already in a batch, or not APPROVED, When I include it, Then 409 and nothing is created.
Given a batch, When I download the CSV, Then it has the exact header, amounts with 2 decimals, and a second download is byte-identical.
Given a batch, When I mark it paid, Then its claims become PAID; marking it paid again returns 409.
Given a non-head user, When they call any payout endpoint, Then 403.

Story: As a finance head, I want a dashboard of spend by category, department and month, policy violations and average approval time on the seeded history, so that I can spot trends and bottlenecks.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given the seeded 3,000 historical claims across 8 departments, When I open the dashboard, Then I see KPIs (total spend, claims, pending, avg approval hours, violations, oldest pending).
Then charts show spend by category, by department and by month (default 6 months), and violations by rule.
Given an employee or manager, When they open the dashboard API, Then 403.
Given Prometheus, When it scrapes /metrics, Then queue size by step and oldest pending hours are exposed.

Story: As a employee, I want to see only my own claims, and finance to see an unalterable history of every action, so that my data stays private and every decision is accountable.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given I am an employee, When I list claims, Then only mine are returned; requesting a colleague's claim or receipt returns 404.
Given any transition, delegation change, policy edit or payout, Then an audit row records actor, on-behalf-of, from/to status, step, comment and time.
Given a database user tries UPDATE or DELETE on audit_log, Then the trigger raises an error.
Given a non-GET request without X-Requested-With: ExpenseFlow, Then 403.

Story: As a finance head, I want policy limits stored as configuration and visible to everyone, with my changes audited, so that a limit can change without a code release.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given a fresh install, When the seed runs, Then policy_rules holds all 13 codes with the defaults in CLAUDE.md, plus 150 employees, 8 departments and 3,000 historical claims.
Given any user, When they open the policy page, Then each rule shows code, description, value and outcome.
Given I change MEAL_DAILY_LIMIT via PUT /api/policy/{code}, When a new claim is submitted, Then the new limit applies, and the audit log shows old and new values.
Given a non-head user, When they call PUT /api/policy/{code}, Then 403.
Business Rule / Decision Ref: Scope 8; Scope 9; all policy codes; TIER1_CITIES

Story: As a employee, I want to be notified when my claim is approved, sent back, rejected or paid (mock outbox), so that I do not have to keep checking the app.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given a status change on my claim, Then a message is written to an outbox table with recipient and template.
Given the outbox page, When I open it, Then I see my notifications newest first.
Policy-edit UI with versioning, OCR of receipts and multi-currency are also stretch and not covered here.
